evidence.quote: Table 8-1 is the new recommended leeway classes and values for the National SAR Manual, GDOC AMM, and CASP.
The seventh column in Table 8-1 is the divergence angle in degrees.
Sub-Table 8-1A (Sub-table for Maritime Life Rafts with Deep Ballast Systems and Canopies)
Sea Kayak W/ Person on aft deck 1.1 12.5 20 3.52 [33]

tried: apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/ADA366414.pdf redirected to DTIC's 'Under Maintenance' page on 21 Oct 2026; the Internet Archive item DTIC_ADA366414 holds the same scanned file (351 pages, no text layer).
The archive's OCR text scrambles the landscape table's columns, so values were read from rendered page images of pp. 8-5, 8-6 and 8-7 (PDF pages 185 to 187) and checked a second time on zoomed crops.
notes: Table 8-1 transcribed for every class the task names: person in water (general, vertical, sitting, three horizontal variants), maritime life rafts (no ballast with and without canopy and drogue; shallow ballast; the 4-6 person deep-ballast sub-table 8-1A with and without drogue, light and heavy loading), an aviation 4-6 person raft, skiffs (flat bottom, V-hull, V-hull swamped), sea kayak and surfboard. Units as printed: slope as a percentage of the 10 m wind speed, y-intercept in cm/s, divergence in degrees, Sy/x in cm/s. The 1999 divergence angles are maximum values; the 2013 SAR Addendum (bundle for leeway-sar-addendum-h7) says it divided them by 1.35 to give average values and converted intercepts to knots, so the two tables must be cited separately. The evacuation slide row prints its capacity as '46-person', which the 2013 table gives as '4-6 person'; not used here. Authors are not named in this bundle per the lab's rule; the report number identifies the document.
